scope: Six new fictional diagnostic scenarios authored by the implementing agent before their first execution. These are transparent regression scenarios, not independent student or predictive-validity evidence. Theme-level official answers intentionally simplify each profile.

cases.name: Morgan · repair first
cases.biography: Enjoys diagnosing faults and replacing worn parts in a workshop. Does not want design iteration or component modeling. Open to college if the work appeals, but pay alone should not turn repair into engineering.

cases.name: Jordan · design and testing
cases.biography: Likes physics, circuit design, comparing component performance and testing prototypes. Has tried a repair workshop but prefers finding design weaknesses. College is welcome.

cases.name: Casey · accurate records
cases.biography: Likes reconciling a small club’s transactions and keeping records accurate. Does not enjoy explaining financial choices or making forecasts. College is an option rather than the goal.

cases.name: Riley · financial explanation
cases.biography: Likes tracing discrepancies, testing assumptions in forecasts, and explaining a financial choice with a budget. Interested in college accounting; routine records alone are not the extent of the interest.

cases.name: Drew · practical food preparation
cases.biography: Enjoys timing a meal, handling several orders, and practising repeatable cooking techniques. Laboratory research is unfamiliar. A food interest should not automatically establish food science.

cases.name: Alex · food quality research
cases.biography: Curious about chemistry, food quality and sources of laboratory error. Prefers controlled samples and careful procedures to a busy kitchen. Wants to consider college science.
